analysis: Only .github/scripts/test-threat-budget.py changed (head lines 949-982 per file_changes, within LifecycleTests). The supplied units are BASE text only; the new tests are visible solely in a truncated patch excerpt (patch_excerpt_complete=false). The additions are CI test-harness code: a manual GitHub rerun handoff (MANUAL_SCAN_RERUN_DISABLED, no paid calls, clean() false), a bounded runtime parser (default 900, max 3000, invalid values rejected), and a Bedrock workload-ceiling handoff test. No provider, coordinator, attestation, cryptographic, or cache code is touched, so the provider-scope threat model (A-001..A-017, TB-002/003/007/009/010/011, T-041 etc.) is not materially affected. The test fixtures use synthetic tokens and a local 127.0.0.1 HTTP server. I identified no new attack surface or regression. Remaining integration question: the tests reference production behavior (runtime_seconds in threat-model-review.py, the Bedrock helpers self.bedrock_run and self.bedrock_response, MANUAL_SCAN_RERUN_DISABLED handling in budget_runner) that is not in the supplied evidence. Whether those controls fail closed (a rerun must not bypass the Ten-PR pilot/budget ledger, and a handoff must keep clean() false) can't be verified from this unit. The tests assert both, which is a positive signal, but the implementation needs review in other batches. The patch excerpt is truncated, so the final assertions of the third test were not seen.
